forbids: recording partial conformance to a method with no deviation stated; escalating a prerequisite of a method whose prerequisites this toolkit cannot see
note: Enrolled with the guard in v0.88.0 (BL-93 B7), covering BL-92's A6 as well as this item's B3. The two halves fail in opposite directions — half 1 stops the register claiming more than it can support, half 2 stops it reporting on work it cannot observe — which is why one mutation each is not enough on its own to prove the suite.

mutations.why: Drop the deviations requirement, which is the single most plausible 'simplify the validation' edit in the file: the check reads like an over-strict extra condition on a field that is already optional, and removing it makes a refusal go away rather than making a test go red. It is BL-92 A6 — the whole design in one check — and nothing else in the suite notices its absence.
defeats: partial conformance with no deviation is refused on write
...and the refusal names the flag, the reason and the naming rule

mutations.why: Remove the external-method boundary, which is the mutation this item most expects to see attempted in earnest. The plan says so outright: the pressure to 'just flag it anyway' will be real, because an escalation looks like value and the suppression is a single early return that reads like dead code. Deleting it makes Monte Carlo, Bayesian, event tree and Open FAIR all escalate on prerequisites nobody here can observe.
defeats: an external method escalates nothing, both conditions true

mutations.why: the write-side boundary removed, so an external method is refused `partial` with no deviations again. This is the pre-BL-238 behaviour, and it is the mutation a future 'surely we should still catch THIS one' change actually makes: the escalation half stays silent under it, so nothing else in this suite notices.
mutations.note: Registered as its own half rather than folded into `external` because the two sites are in different functions and fail in different directions — one is a refusal at write, the other an escalation at read. A single half would have meant one mutation could not distinguish them.
defeats: an external method is NOT refused partial with no deviations (BL-238)
...and the uncaveated record is actually stored, not dropped
...and set-method says the fields are recorded but not checked
